pagerbot: :rotating_light: P1 PAGE 1DB1  - Canary rollout triggered a schema change that rewrote 'orders' (stored generated column). Auto-page to on-call.

pagerbot: Affected service: orders-db-primary. Symptoms: canary hosts returning 502/timeout on checkout, replication lag > 50s, write queue growing. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/db-migration-hang>.

deploy-bot: deploy started by sana at 2026-03-15T08:45:12Z. Canary = 2%. Predeploy migration job: migrations/2026_03_add_stored_total_cents.sql -> status: RUNNING (pid 66321).

harper: oncall-sre acknowledging. Pulling pg_stat_activity and logs. Seeing backend 66321 running a long ALTER TABLE that appears to be rewriting orders. IO is saturated, wal bytes spiking.

noah: from app logs: canary returns 502s for /v1/orders and checkout endpoints. Routing shows ~2% of traffic hitting canary. CS flags show ~57 failed checkout attempts so far.

sana: original migration SQL from migration-runner:
```sql
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN total_amount_cents integer GENERATED ALWAYS AS (floor(total_amount * 100)) STORED;
COMMIT;
```
This is a stored generated column (STORED) which triggers a full table rewrite on Postgres 13. That explains the lock and WAL churn.

harper: psql snapshot:
```
pid    | state  | query
66321  | active | ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN total_amount_cents integer GENERATED ALWAYS AS (floor(total_amount * 100)) STORED;
66345  | idle   | SELECT 1
```
`ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN ... STORED` is the culprit.

mike: mitigation options: 1) cancel the query (pg_cancel_backend) and hope it releases quickly; 2) kill the backend (SIGKILL) to free locks; 3) flip feature flag to stop canary writes so new requests won't hit the path; 4) roll canary back and ensure migration-runner is aborted; 5) promote a replica for canary traffic if needed.

sana: I rolled the canary back via Console right after errors started but, as usual, migration-runner didn't stop. Rolling back app doesn't abort separate migration jobs.

harper: agree. Let's flip the feature flag to be safe while we attempt to cancel the migration.

noah: customer impact assessment: primarily new-order and checkout endpoints. ~2% of users (canary cohort) saw failures between 08:45:12Z and now. We'll need CS outreach for ~57 failed attempts. No payment capture failures reported.

mike: executing cancel: `SELECT pg_cancel_backend(66321);` -> returns true, but pg_locks still shows relation lock on orders. If it doesn't release in 25s, we'll SIGKILL.

sana: flipping flag now: `redwood-flags disable new_pricing_v1 --scope=canary`

sana: feature flag flip success at 2026-03-15T08:47:05Z. Canary hosts should fall back.

harper: cancel didn't free lock. Issuing `kill -9 66321` in 10s. Be aware killing a rewrite can leave partial on-disk state or temp files; ops-bot shows last base backup at 2026-03-15T01:40Z.

harper: `kill -9 66321` executed. Process terminated. WAL generation dropped ~72%. Replication lag falling: 52s -> 9s over 75s.

sana: verifying replicas: three replicas reported caught-up <3s within 4 minutes. Good.

noah: app-side: canary 502s drop immediately after FF flip and kill. Production traffic unaffected. Recovery window ~3-4 minutes.

mike: scanning DB: leftover temp table `orders__gencol_tmp_20260315` ~28GB present. It's not locked but occupies space. We'll schedule a cleanup job to DROP it after ensuring no dependent objects. Also checking for partial column metadata.

harper: checking schema: `pg_attribute` shows `total_amount_cents` absent (migration aborted cleanly by kill), no new type objects found. Good. Need to run a quick checksum on recent PK ranges to be sure no partial data corruption.

cs-kate: summarizing impact for CS handoff:
- What: Canary deploy triggered a stored generated column addition which rewrote the orders table and blocked writes.
- Who: ~2% traffic (canary) experienced checkout/new-order failures (estimated ~57 requests) between 08:45:12Z - 08:48:30Z. No confirmed payment capture failures; most were client timeouts.
- Mitigation: feature-flag disable (sana), migration query canceled and then killed (harper/mike), canary rolled back (sana). Replication returned to healthy within minutes.
- Data integrity: no data loss found in cursory checks; we'll run full PK range checksum as follow-up.
- Next steps: cleanup temp artifacts, rework migration to a no-rewrite pattern (add nullable column without STORED or add plain column + backfill in chunks + convert to STORED in a maintenance window), add migration-runner preflight to detect STORED/generated columns or other table-rewrite operations and block during canary, tie migration lifecycle to deploy rollback (auto-abort), and add safety lint to CI.

sana: creating follow-up tickets now:
- INF-3401 cleanup leftover gencol temp table and reclaim storage
- INF-3402 migration-runner preflight: detect STORED/generated columns & table rewrites (block on canary)
- INF-3403 migration pattern: support chunked backfill + safe conversion to STORED in maintenance window
- INF-3404 add automatic abort hook when a deployment rollback is triggered

harper: I'll own the postmortem write-up and coordinate schema team. Tentative postmortem scheduled 2026-03-16 14:00 UTC.

oncall-sre: handing off monitoring to noah for daytime follow-up. I'll remain available for escalations.

pagerbot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> follow-up tasks created. P1 downgraded to P2 for remediation. Postmortem scheduled.

sana: thanks team, will update the status page and coordinate CS outreach. :thumbsup:
